lines.t: Hoo! Welcome to Eastside, {name}. Last time you fixed the Foot Bridge and chased the Smudge across it.
Do you still have that gray brick chip stamped with a G? Keep it safe. I think the Smudge came this way.
That big building is the General Store. Mrs. Mabel weighs everything she sells. Go say hello.
Gray fuzz that smells like hay. Next time we climb to the Hilltop Dairy, {name}.
Hoo! Every store job on the page helps Mrs. Mabel open for the day.
Hoo! Gray fuzz, just like the Smudge. And it smells like hay.
Hay means cows, and cows mean the Hilltop Dairy. Keep the fuzz with your brick chip, {name}. Next lesson, we climb the hill.

lines.t: Oh, hello, dear! I'm Mrs. Mabel. This is my General Store.
Last night the Smudge came through. It knocked my scale and smudged three of my labels!
Every label shows a weight in pounds and ounces. Please find the three smudged ones and fix them. Walk onto a sparkle to read one.
Every label is right again. Thank you, {name}!
Now I can open the store. Come back and help me with orders later.
Your basket order was perfect! But my big scale still has a crooked needle.
The Smudge bent it. Please set it right with my 1-pound test weight. The scale is out front on the plaza.
Here is the rice that was left in the sack: 2 lb 12 oz.
Baker Lou bakes rice bread. Please take it to him by the bakery, up the little path.
Thank you for fixing my price board! But look at that sack by my door.
Its label says 2 lb 19 oz. I never wrote that. Can a label even say that? Please fix it.
Welcome to the General Store, dear! Everything here is weighed in pounds and ounces.
Good as new! Now weigh this bag: 1 lb 10 oz of cashews, and I'm adding 9 oz of pecans.
2 pounds 3 ounces on the dot! My scale is as good as new.
Read my Scale Board on your page, then help me with the rice sack.
